parties:
Zahir Akhter (Md) and 44 anothers ------- Petitioners
Vs. 
Bangladesh Biman Corporation and another ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
AFM Abdur Rahman J: In these Rules, issued in Writ Petition Nos. 5268 of 2007, 5270 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5271 of 2007, Writ Petition 191 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 1023-24 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 4203 of 2007 Writ Petition No. 1447 of 07, Writ Petition No. 5269 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 6285 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 6284 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5076 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5073 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5074 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5072 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5075 of 2007. Writ Petition No. 1779 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 2031 of 2007 in one set and Writ Petition Nos. 1111 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 1112 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 2486 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 7923 of 2007 in the second set, Writ Petition Nos. 2853 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 2854 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 2855 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 2856 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5006 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5007 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5008 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5009 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 5010 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 3773 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 3662 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 4470 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 4712 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 7986 of 2007 in the third set, Writ Petition Nos. 1642 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 3146 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 3145 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 4114 of 2007 in the fourth set, Writ Petition Nos. 10556 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 9677 of 2007, Writ Petition No. 8892 of 2007 in the fifth set. Writ Petition Nos. 2410 of 2007 and Writ Petition No. 2411 of 2007 in the sixth set involve the termination employees of Bangladesh Biman, having the same cause of action involving similar question of law and facts have been heard together and now disposed of by this single judgment.

2. The aforesaid Rules Nisi were issued on different date in the month of May, 2007 at the instance of the writ petitioners, calling upon the respondents Bangladesh Biman Corporation represented by the Managing Director and other two functionaries of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation to show cause as to why the impugned order of termination of the writ petitioners, disclosed in various impugned annexures appended to the writ petitions, should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or to pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. The facts, of the aforesaid writ petitions are similar. The petitioners while serving in the Bangladesh Biman Corporation in different posts having completed the service for not less than 20 years, were terminated by the Biman authority, without assigning any reason purportedly in exercise of the power available under Regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation 1979. The writ petitioners assail the termination order in the writ petitions stating, inter alia, their service against the permanent post in the Bangladesh Biman Corporation since been confirmed on various dates and they have completed considerable years of service in different promoted posts have been illegally terminated by the Biman Authority. It has been further asserted that no allegation has been raised against the writ petitioners at any point of time during their long service record and even no iota of dissatisfaction has ever been shown by the Biman Corporation against the writ petitioners in respect of their high standard of professional capacity. The Bangladesh Biman Corporation is a statutory public authority within the meaning of Article 152 of the Constitution and an employee of Biman is a public servant. The Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation, 1979 is applicable to their service and under the provision of Regulation 11 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations 1979 the writ petitioners are entitled to retire from service upon completion of 57 years of their age or on attaining the age of superannuation by the writ petitioners. The writ petitioners are on the verge of attaining age of superannuation and only a year or two is ahead of their retirement and when they are waiting to retire usually from the service, they have been terminated with malafide intention from the service of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation. The Bangladesh Biman Corporation was constituted under the provision of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance 1977 (Ordinance No. XIX of 1977) which was amended through Bangladesh Biman Corporation (Amendment) Ordinance 2007 with effect from 11-7-2007 which by incorporating section 28A provided for conversion of Bangladesh Biman Corporation into a public limited company and accordingly, through SRO No. 191-Law12007 dated 31-7-2007 the Bangladesh Biman Corporation was abolished and the same has been reconstituted as a public limited company (PLC) under the Companies Act 1994 with effect from 23-7-2007.

4. It has been further stated in a supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioners that there had been a steering committee formed by the government to deal with the interest of the employees of the Biman with the government and on 8-8-2000 the Biman Authority had entered into a memorandum of understanding, which was signed by the director (admin) of Biman in presence of the Secretary. Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, wherein it has been clearly, laid down the decision that no employee of Biman shall be retrenched unless declared redundant as per labour law. But suddenly Biman terminated and compulsorily retired about 147 officers and employees (compulsorily retired 81 and terminated 66), without assigning any reason, between the period of October 2006 to April 2007. Thereafter, Biman came out with a scheme known as voluntary retirement scheme (VRS) on 4 June 2007 and offered 2000 employees of Biman to avail the opportunity of VRS on the ground of restructuring of Biman to make it profitable and viable as an International Air Carrier.

5. It has been further asserted that although the Biman has decided to reduce its work force and opted for illegal termination of the employees, yet the Biman is making appointment afresh in those posts in which the petitioners were employees, apparently on the contract basis and on higher pay. Such illegal activity of the Biman having serious implication in the society, attracting the attention of the media, the government had constituted a review committee on 2-1-2008, which by its report dated 17-4-2008 categorically mentioned that serious irregularities have been committed in dealing with the matter the employees by the Biman authority. It has been asserted that the persons who have opted for VRS, which has been allowed to 1876 employees, just within three months of the termination of the 66 officers of Biman, has received each Taka 20,00,000 (twenty lac) from Biman as a benefit for accepting such VRS. On the other hand, the 66 terminated officers, including the petitioners, had not been allowed any kind of benefit even the minimum benefit of the notice pay, as embodied in Regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations 1979. Challenging such termination of the writ petitioners from the service of Biman Corporation the instant Rules were obtained on different dates by the writ petitioners.

6. Pursuant to the service of the Rule the learned Advocates Mr Mushfiqur Rahman Khan, Mr Joynal Abedin entered appearance on behalf of the respondents in different Writ petitions. Both the learned Advocates submitted affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-opposition.

7. It has been asserted in the affidavit-in- opposition that the Bangladesh Biman Corporation was a statutory corporation, constituted under the Provision of Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance 1977 (Ordinance XIX of 1977) which adopted its employees service regulation in the year 1979 under the name and style Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation 1979. The writ petitioners being the employees of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation are amenable to the provision of the said regulation and when the Biman Corporation was a losing concern, the government had decided to restructure the said corporation in various ways in order to make the concern viable and profitable at with International Airlines. But all ways and means since did not work or appeared to be inadequate, the government decided to reduce the number of employees of the Biman and other work force for the streamlining of the office administration to protect and preserve the organisation's smooth functioning and accordingly, in exercise of power under Regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation 1979 the writ petitioners were terminated from the service and were given the appropriate benefit to which they were entitled under the Regulation 52. The said Regulation 52 was never used by the Biman authority arbitrarily, injudiciously and capriciously which was taken by the Board of Directors of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation and duly approved by the government. The said Regulation 52 did not provide for any prior notice before exercising the power under the said regulation and the same is not violative of the provision of Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution. The said power under Regulation 52 is a common standard power, preserved for the purpose to meet the contingency in management of the service of the excess and not required employees, not only in the Bangladesh Biman Corporation but also in all statutory corporations as well as non statutory bodies.

8. It has been further stated that Regulation 59 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation 1979 provides for appeal by the aggrieved employees of the Biman Corporation against his termination, which having not been availed by the writ petitioners, the instant writ petitions are not maintainable on the principle of rule of exhaustion.

9. It has also been stated that the Bangladesh Biman Corporation since transformed into a public limited company, the instant Rules are not maintainable against such body, rather the same has became infructuous due to the transformation of the statutory body into a public limited company, Moreover, the termination, as assailed by the writ petitioners are termination simpliciter, which cannot be assailed on the ground of non-compliance of rules of natural justice. The Biman Corporation since became a public limited company, the rules of master and servant is-now applicable as a guiding principle for the service of employees and, as such, the Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited is not liable to take back any employees who were terminated by the predecessor statutory body under its lawful provision of the service regulation. Therefore, the instant Rules are liable to be discharged.

10. Out of this six sets of writ petitions, the writ petitioners are represented by the learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon appearing for the first group, the learned Advocate Mr Abdul Based Majumder with the learned Advocate Mr Abu Sayed Ahmed represented the second group while the learned Advocate Mr AKM Nazrul Islam represented the 3rd group, the learned Advocate Mr Hasan Foez Siddique appeared for the petitioner in the 4th group, while the learned Advocate Mr Swapon Kumar Dutta represented the 5th group and the learned Advocate Mr KS Nabi argued on behalf of the writ petitioners in the 6th group. On the other hand, the learned Advocate Mr Mushfiqur Rahman Khan and Mr Joynal Abedin remain present on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 and the learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam argued on their behalf.

11. The grounds as taken in these writ petitions are more or less similar. The learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon while assailed the termination of the writ petitioners takes this Court through the respective date of joining of the writ petitioners in the erstwhile Bangladesh Biman Corporation and indicates that the writ petitioners while on the verge of completion of 25 years of their service and expended .their golden period of life in the successful service of Biman, they have been terminated in an illegal exercise of the power under Regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations 1979. The learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon argues that although the power under Regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Employees (Service) Regulation 1979 is exercisable without assigning any reason, yet the respondents were under obligation to assign reason since provision for non-assigning any reason for termination under the provision of Regulation 52 does not mean that the termination can be made without any reason.

12. The learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon strenuously argues that while the writ petitioners have almost completed 25 years of their service upon which they will get their full retirement benefit, the respondents in order to deprive the writ petitioners from their legitimate rights, exercised the power under Regulation 52 of the service regulation most arbitrarily and with a malafide intention, which is clearly revealed from the subsequent decision of the respondents to recruit incumbents in the same post under contractual basis and, as such, the termination of the petitioners must be treated as having been made without lawful authority.

13. The learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon next argues that the writ petitioners after their appointment in the Bangladesh Biman Corporation successfully completed their probation period against the permanent post of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation and the authority having been satisfied about their performance confirmed their service in the permanent post, meaning thereby that the confirmed employees of the Bangladesh Biman shall not lose their job unless only through a disciplinary proceeding taken against them else the termination must be termed as arbitrary and capricious. The learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon contends that otherwise the concept of confirmation of the incumbent against the permanent post as will be nugatory one if the power available under Regulation 52 is allowed to be exercised against a confirmed employee of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation without any reason. Therefore, in accordance with the learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon, the termination of the writ petitioners are not only arbitrary exercise of the power under Regulation 52 of the Service Regulation but also tainted with illegality and malafide.

14. The learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon draws the attention of this Court to various decisions of the Apex Court of our jurisdiction and also from the Indian jurisdiction in order to substantiate his arguments that such exercise of power of termination simpliciter has already been decided by the Apex Court as arbitrary, having no guideline and prone to be used in a discriminatory manner and, as such, the same power cannot be exercised without specific reason and since the cause raised in this writ petitions have already been decided by the Apex Court in various judgments, these Rules are required to be made absolute.

15. In this context the learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon also relied upon some unreported case namely, Shamsul Hoq vs Chairman, BADC in Writ Petition No. 6071 of 2003, the Employees Union, BADC vs Chairman, BADC in Writ Petition No. 4098 of 2003 and 5630 of 2002, the case of the Chairman, BADC vs Employee Union BADC and Shamsul Hoq in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 158-184 of 2006 with Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 136 of 2007 which has been subsequently reported in 60 DLR (AD) 152(1), the case of Dr ATM Nazmul Akhter vs Secretary, BGME in Writ Petition No. 4560 of 2002, the case of the Secretary, BGME vs SAH Monowar in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.354 of 2004, Chairman BCIC vs MA Salam in CPLA No. 1317-1321 of 2005 and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1419-1424 of 2005, the case of AB Siddique vs Chairman, BPAPC in Writ Petition No.1986 of 1999 and Writ Petition No. 116 of 2000, the case of CM Yousuf vs Bangladesh Biman in WP No.553 of 1976, the Case of Bangladesh Biman vs KM A laud din in CR No. 963 of 2000, the case of Bangladesh Biman vs KM Alauddin in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1935 of 2001, the case of Md Obaidul Gani vs Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS) in Writ Petition No. 2104 of 2002.

16. The learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon further relies on the cases decided in the Indian jurisdiction, specially the case of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd vs Brojo Nath reported in AIR 1986 (SC) 1571.

17. While adopting the arguments of the learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon the learned Advocate Mr AKM Nazrul Islam representing the 3rd group of the writ petitioners, assails the termination of the writ petitioners on the ground that the exercise of power under regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation 1979 has not given a power to the Biman authority to exercise the same against the confirmed employees of the Biman in a manner which adversely affects the confirmed employees without any allegation or stigma, when they were about to complete their 25 years of service, as the same employees cannot be treated as obliged by the mercy of the Biman authority that they can fire the employees as and when they so wish.

18. The learned Advocate Mr AKM Nazrul Islam in contemplation of the prospective argument which may be advanced by the Biman's learned Advocates as to non availing of the efficacious remedy further argues that no question of preferring any efficacious remedy by way of appeal against the termination of the employees comes at all since the provision of Regulation 59 of the Biman Service Regulation does not provide for any appeal for the employees terminated under the provision of Regulation 52 and the provision for appeal is only applicable when there is a disciplinary action against any of the employees on the basis of allegation and, as such, the rule of exhaustion has no manner of application in this writ petition and these writ petitions are squarely maintainable without such filing of appeal, although the writ petitioners, to avoid any complication submitted an application under Regulation 59 of the Service Regulation 1979 to the higher authority of the Biman Corporation which has not yet been disposed of by the Biman authority which also indicates the malafide intention of the respondents.

19. The learned Advocate Mr AM Nazrul Islam further develops his argument on the point of transformation of Biman into a public limited company and strenuously argues that the present Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited is the same entity alike the erstwhile statutory corporation, despite the trans formation of its status as a public limited company and, as such, the reinstatement of the writ petitioners shall have no adverse affect on the smooth administration of the Biman as a public limited company.

20. The learned Advocate Mr AKM Nazrul Islam further argues that despite the fact of termination of the petitioners from the service of the post of Biman, the Biman is now further recruiting persons in the same post upon contractual basis which clearly manifests that the requirement of the writ petitioners in the present Biman set-up has not been exhausted and since the petitioners are victim of pick and choose rule in respect of firing under the provision of Regulation 52, of the Biman Employees Service Regulation the equity requires that the writ petitioners are reinstated in their respective post in the new structure of Bangladesh Biman. The learned Mr AKM Nazrul Islam contends that the writ petitioners served the Biman for not less then 22-25 years and while they were waiting to undergo the provision of usual retirement with entitlement to full benefit, have been deprived of their all legitimate rights as they were forced to go home without having any benefit from the Biman, even the notice pay, which has been mentioned in Regulation 52 as has to be paid to the writ petitioners. Therefore, as this Court is also a Court of equity, shall look into the substance of the case and render appropriate redress to the writ petitioners.

21. The learned Advocate Mr AKM Nazrul Islam relied upon the case reported in 7 DLR (SC) 91 and 33 DLR (AD) 321 and also the case of Uptron India Limited vs Shammi Bhan reported in AIR 1998 (SC) 1681, the case reported in AIR 1986 (SC) 1571, AIR 1991 (SC) 537, AIR 1991 (SC) 101, AIR 1964 (SC) 600, AIR 1985 (SC) 1046, AIR 1986 (SC) 1108 and AIR 1990 (SC) 307.

22. The learned Advocate Mr KS Nabi, representing the 6th group of the writ petitioners, heavily assails the termination of the writ petitioner on the point that the impugned termination is practically a dismissal, since the undisclosed reason behind such termination is to downsizing the Biman work force and, as such, the writ petitioners were entitled to appropriate notice prior to their termination from the service in order to explain their position. He submits that even this termination has been passed by the Board of Directors of the Biman Corporation, yet it is a clear instance of pick and choose policy, since the provision of Regulation 52 did not provide for any prescribed method of ascertaining how the same power can be exercised amongst the employees on the face of the fact that within two months of the termination of the writ petitioners, a bulk of the employees of the Bangladesh Biman has been offered the Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) which allowed the said employees to obtain a handsome monetary compensation which is not less than Taka 20 lac to each employee, when the writ petitioners have been deprived of not only such benefit but even the benefit of notice.

23. The learned Advocate Mr KS Nabi further assails the Regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation 1979 as having contradicted the Biman Corporation Ordinance, 1977 since, the same is a protected legislation as it is included in the constitution and, as such, the power incorporated in Regulation 52 of the said service regulation is inconsistent with the parent legislation Bangladesh Biman Corporation Order, 1977.

24. The learned Advocate Mr KS Nabi finally argues that the power available under Regulation 52 of the Service Regulation, 1979 is only to be exercised against the apprentices probationers, temporary employees, part time employees substitutes and casual employees against whom the Biman is entitled to terminate without serving any notice because the term 'confirmed against the perm anent post has the essence of permanency, meaning there- by that the incumbent has been put to the guarantee of service tenure and shall not lose his job on any other ground than the provision of service regulation. The learned Advocate Mr KS Nabi contends that the employees of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation since liable to the disciplinary action under the Regulation 55, the only procedure for discharging an employee of the Bangladesh Biman available it to start disciplinary proceeding against the said employee. Therefore, the exercise of power under Regulation 52 of the service regulation is nothing but a colourable exercise of power purportedly under the statute which must be termed as a malafide action on the part of the respondents.

25. The learned Advocate Mr Abdul Baset Majumder representing the second group of the writ petitioners also adopted the argument of Mr Salauddin Dolon with an addition that the provision of Regulation 52 is a harsh one which cannot be applied against the confirmed employees of Bangladesh Biman as the same has no guideline as to its particular exercise against the category of the employees and, as such, the said provision has given an arbitrary power to the Biman authority to pick and choose a person and, as such, the termination of the writ petitioners in exercise of the said power must be decided to have been exercised without lawful authority.

26. The learned Advocate Abdul Baset Majumder further argues that such a power as incorporated in Regulation 52 of the employees service regulation of Biman was not contended in the parent legislation and since the subordinate legislation has provided a contradictory power, the same is also liable to be struck down and, as such, the termination of the writ petitioners, in exercise of the said discriminatory provision of the service regulation must be termed as exercised without any lawful authority.

27. The learned Advocate Mr Hasan Foez Siddique who represented the 4th group of the writ petitioners also adopted the arguments of the learned Advocates representing the other groups.

28. The learned Advocate Mr Swapon Kumar Dutta represented the 5th group of the petitioners also adopted the arguments of the learned Advocate representing the other groups.

29. On the other hand, the learned Advocate Mr Akhter Imam, while refuting the arguments of the learned Advocates representing the writ petitioners, relies upon a number of decisions of both home and abroad and while takes this Court through the history of the constituting legislature of Bangladesh Biman Corporation, draws the attention of this Court to the fact that the Bangladesh Biman Corporation while inundated in debt and mismanagement the government decided to streamline its administration through primarily reducing its work force from 6837 to 3400 for saving its expenses in this respect and accordingly, the Biman decided in its Board of Directors meeting to pave the way of such reducing of number of employees by adopting different means out of which termination of the employees, voluntarily retirement scheme (VRS), etc have been adopted as the procedure for such downsizing the work force. Accordingly, Biman Corporation invited applications from the employees for availing the VRS and under such scheme 1877 employees obtained the benefit of such scheme. But prior to such adaptation of VRS scheme, the other procedure for downsizing the work force has been applied and since the writ petitioners were redundant in the service of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation, they have been terminated in exercise of the power available under the Regulation 52(i) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Ser.) Regulation 1979.

30. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam categorically argues that nothing illegality has been committed by the Biman authority in terminating the writ petitioners under the lawful provision of the employees service regulation which has been formulated and adopted under the provision of the parent law the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance 1977 to meet such contingency which is a beneficial provision for the employer.

31. In expounding such contention, the learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam indicates that Regulation 52 as embodied in Biman service regulation is an enabling provision available to the employer to get rid of any employee who is required to be deducted from the work force and against whom no allegation or stigma is available. The learned Senior Counsel argues that such a power is also available in all the statutory corporations' service rule, prevailing in Bangladesh, formulated in the wisdom of the law makers for the beneficial and efficient operation of the statutory corporation. Because, unless such power is available to the employer of the statutory corporation, the contingency that could arise from time to time in respect of excess employee, cannot be coup lied with and therefore the power under Regulation 52 of the Biman's Employees Service Regulation, 1979 is a beneficial one for which a series of decisions of the Court and the apex Courts of home and aboard have already decided that the same is not ultra vires to the constitution.

32. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam continues arguing that a consensus view of the Apex Court of Bangladesh has already made it a rule of law and the precedent became a stare decisis that termination simpliciter cannot be interfered with in judicial review since, the power under which such termination simpliciter is made, had never violated any of the provision of the parent legislation. Moreover, it was decided by the Apex Court that the rule of natural justice is not also applicable, while the employer decides to exercise power under such provision.

33. The learned Advocate Mr Akhter Imam specifically takes this Court through the provision of Regulation 52 of the Biman Service Regulation 1979 and strenuously argues that the said provision has allowed the employer to pay the employee money in lieu of notice and accordingly, the Biman authority complied the provision of the said .Regulation 52 and offered the notice pay to the writ petitioners as terminated employees of the Biman, along with their usual benefit as to gratuity, provident fund, etc. which comes for an employee completing 10 years of service, at not less than Taka six lac.

34. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam further argues that the instant writ petitions have become infructuous, if not they are non-maintainable, since the Biman has been converted into a public limited company, pursuant to the board meeting dated 25-3-2007 and the statutory corporation was abolished on 31-7-2007, wherefrom a new entity named Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited came into existence and that being a public limited company, is not amenable to the jurisdiction of Article 102 of the Constitution. Therefore, although the Rule has been issued prior to the formation of the PLC, yet since there is no existence of the statutory corporation, these Rules are liable to be discharged as being infructuous.

35. The learned Senior Counsel further argues that the rule of master and servant is applicable henceforth in case of Biman employee and since the service of the employee of a private organisation depends on the requirement by the employer, the terminated employees of the Biman, including the writ petitioners, cannot be thrust upon the shoulder of the Biman authority , as no writ of mandamus can be asked to be issued against a public limited company.

36. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam in support of his argument relies upon the case reported in AIR 1969 (SC) 1307.

37. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam vehemently argues that from the formation of Biman as a PLC, the government has no supervisory or regulatory authority upon the Biman and although none of the shares of the government have been floated in the stock exchange for public listing, yet the Biman shall not be amenable to the jurisdiction of Article 102 of the Constitution.

38. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam takes this Court through decisions reported in 29 DLR (SC) 29, 31 DLR (AD) 303, 33 DLR 300, 43 DLR (AD) 154, 46 DLR (AD) 1 and draws the attention of the Court to the case reported in 60 DLR (AD) 152(1) and argues that the same has not decided particularly the termination illegal, rather it was decided in that case that the provision of the termination clause was not complied with, Moreover, the learned Senior Counsel Mr Imam argues, that the decision has been passed per incuriam as all the earlier otherwise decisions have not been cited before the apex Court and, as such, the question as to the authority of the employer to exercise power under the provision of termination simpliciter has not been considered in the light of the earlier decisions.

39. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam further argues that to make Biman a profitable concern, restructuring of its personnel department was required and in order to benefit the workers of Biman the terminated employees have been paid Taka 6,00,000 (six lac) each including' all benefits which is no less than the payment made to the employees who have availed the VRS scheme. Such an attempt to restructure the personnel department has not only been done in Biman, but also in other statutory corporations, specially BJMC, BADC, Dhaka Electric Supply Authority (DESA) and other statutory corporations have exercised the termination simpliciter provisions of their employees service rules, which was ultimately declared by this Court, in various writ petitions as lawful. The learned Senior Counsel contends that termination of service simpliciter without giving any stigma or making any accusation, not being a punishment as contemplated under Regulation 52(i) of Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation, 1979. The question of any grievance for breach of the principles of natural justice for not giving notice or opportunity of being heard does not arise, irrespective of the nature of the service of the petitioners, which is permanent in nature.

40. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam further vehemently argues that if the termination of service is found to be within the four comers of the law, the Court cannot nullify it on the ground that it is harsh or unjust.

41. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam while takes this Court through the internet addition of different news media draws the attention of this Court to the fact that the same procedure has also been adopted by other International Airlines, specially the British Airways and the airlines of the United State of America and German Democratic Republic. Therefore, according to the learned Advocate, Mr Akhter Imam, nothing has prejudiced the terminated employees as the Biman authority has exercised a lawful power available under the provision of service regulation.

42. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam finally argues that even if this Court finds that the termination simpliciter cannot be sustained, yet the reinstatement of the writ petitioners cannot be ordered since the same shall not only open the flood gate but also prejudice the Biman authority adversely as the whole restructuring scheme of the Biman, which already made the national flag carrier a profitable concern, shall be frustrated and, as such, the writ petitioners can only be allowed to avail damage against the employer, which shall not effect the present Biman authority, since the earlier statutory corporation was controlled by the government itself and the liability of the writ petitioners shall be borne by the government. The learned Advocate Mr Akhter Imam prays for discharge of the Rules.

43. We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the writ petitions, the supplementary affidavits filed by the writ petitioners, the affidavit-in- opposition, the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition and the annexures appended thereto. We have also perused the materials on record and the documents submitted at the time of hearing. The arguments of the learned Advocates have also been considered in their true perspective.

44. Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited, as it stands now, is a public limited company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994 on 23rd day of July 2007. This national flag carrier was originally constituted under the President Order No. 2 of 1972 which was subsequently re-enacted as President Order No. 31 of 1972 (PO 31 of 72) which was finally amended by the President Order No. 126 of 1972. This new flag carrier of newly horn Bangladesh has taken over the assets and liabilities of the eastern wing of the Pakistan International Airlines Corporation (PIAC) situated in the then East Pakistan now Bangladesh. The employees and liabilities of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) were taken for the purpose of efficient operation of the new Airlines in the new born country Bangladesh. Later in the year 1977 the law relating to the national flag carrier was totally modified though the new ordinance named Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance, 1977 (Ordinance No. XIX of 1977) with effect from 9 June, 1977. Under this law the national flag carrier was a statutory corporation being controlled by the government under the relevant ministry, Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism. In the said corporation, the writ petitioners obtained job at different times and carried on with the same for not less than 20 years.

45. It appears from materials on record that the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance 1977 was amended through Ordinance No. 13 of 2007 with effect from 11-7-2007, incorporating section 28A which provided for conversion of Bangladesh Biman Corporation into a public limited company with further provision for abolition at the existing statutory corporation. Accordingly, by the circular being SRO No. 191 (Law) of 2007 dated 31-7-2007 Bangladesh Biman Corporation was abolished on and from 31-7-2007 and on the same date a public limited company Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited was decided to be incorporated under the provision of Companies Act, 1994.

46. While this was going on, the Board of Directors of the Biman Corporation decided to downsize the work force by terminating the writ petitioners and accordingly, in the month of June 2007, the writ petitioners were terminated under the provision of Regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation 1979 on one hand and on the other hand, just after two months, another 1877 employees of Biman were offered the benefit under voluntary retirement scheme (VRS). It has been argued by the learned Advocates in a concerted voice on behalf of the writ petitioners, that while the writ petitioners were only offered the notice pay as provided under Regulation 52 of the Service Regulation, the employees who obtained the opportunity of VRS immediately after two months of the termination of the petitioners on 4-6-2007, obtained a handsome amount from the VRS Scheme which, according to the learned Advocate, as not less than Taka 20,00,000 (twenty lac) each, Later, the Biman became a Public Limited Company on and from its date of incorporation on 23-7-2007 and the Bangladesh Biman Corporation was abolished on 31-7-2007.

47. The learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon, appearing for the writ petitioner, claimed that by the efficient and high professional skill of the writ petitioners, along with other employees of Bangladesh Biman Corporation, the National flag carrier was running as a profitable concern, but due to the unbridled corruption and other malpractice in the upper level of Biman Corporation, it has gradually become a losing concern, the responsibility of which cannot be attributed on the shoulder of the employees of Biman Corporation to make them scapegoats and to terminate them en masse. The learned Advocate Mr Akhter Imam, appearing on behalf of the Bangladesh Biman argued that in order to enhance the image of Biman as a national flag carrier in the International Airlines arena and to make the concern viable and profitable, a restructuring in the whole concern was required and accordingly the government, from time to time, attempted to restructure the Biman, specially in its Human Resources Department. Although in the year 1984 a committee, headed by Mr Enam Ahamed Chowdhury, known as Enam Committee, recommended for the enhancement of the work force of Biman to 6883 personnel for efficient running of the Biman, but at that time the strength of the employees of Biman was only 5600 personnel. But later it was decided by the government to even reduce the said less work force in Biman and also decided to make the statutory corporation into a public limited company for which it was required to resort to the provision of Regulation 52 of the Employee Service Regulation. All this submission and admission indicates that the Biman Corporation decided to reduce the working personnel in it and, as such, exercised the power under Regulation 52 to achieve such end which now appears to be a case of termination enmasse.

48. Now the pertinent question to be resolved by this Court is whether the termination simpliciter enmasse as was made by the Biman Corporation against the writ petitioners was lawful.

49. In the recent past various statutory corporations of Bangladesh were restructured due to the requirement of efficient functioning and smooth operation of the said corporations and accordingly, those statutory corporations have also downsized their manpower by way of termination simpliciter which have been challenged by the affected persons before this division in various writ petitions, as referred by the learned Advocate Mr Salauddin Dolon, particularly the Writ Petition No. 1498 of 2002, heard along with Writ Petition No. 5630 of 2002, in which a Division Bench of this Court passed the Judgment through his Lordship Mr Justice Refat Ahmed, who examined the legality and propriety of the power of termination simpliciter, under the provision of Rule 55(2) of the BJMC Service Rules and held as under:

"This Court found that though the BJMC enjoys the right to terminate under the Rules, it has exercised that right vis-a-vis 200 officers without a rational basis."

50. In the said case his Lordship ultimately also decided that the decision of termination simpliciter was a clear manifestation of gross abuse of power which was made without lawful authority.

51. As against this decision of the High Court Division, a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 354 of 2004 has been preferred by the BJMC, the judgment of which has been reported in 5 LG (AD) 249 in the November, 2008 issue, wherein their Lordships in the Apex Court have decided in the following term:

"We have already said hereinbefore that termination of the service of an employee in the background of Rule 55(2) of the Probidhan Mala contemplates a situation which is absent in the instant case. Thus situation in the background of which BGMC may resort to the Provision of Rule 55(2) of the Probidhan Mala being absent and that as writ-petitioners, service' was terminated in a different context, we are of the view that the High Court Division has committed no error in declaring the action of the petitioner herein as not fair and reasonable. The accepted principle is, that in taking action against an employee in any given situation the employer is to demonstrate fairness in its action and justification in support of the action so taken."

In view of the aforesaid decision, this Court notes that the contemplated situation provided in the provision of termination simpliciter is a pertinent question to be resolved in deciding the legality and propriety of exercise of the power which must be looked into in order to ascertain whether the employer has demonstrated fairness and justification in exercising the said power available under the regulation of termination simpliciter.

52. In another referred writ petition involving BADC being Writ Petition No. 6071 of 2003, a Division Bench of this Court comprised by Mr Justice ABM Khairul Hoque and Mr Justice ATM Fazle Kabir, while deciding a similar question of termination simpliciter exercised by the BADC authority, has categorically come to the decision that the power available under Rule 52(2) of the BADC Service Regulation 1990 cannot be applied in a discriminatory manner and accordingly, decided that this provision allowing termination of service "although may be made either through issuance of a notice in advance for a period of three months or payment of salary for three months to the concerned employee, but it appears that even that minimum requirement of the provision was not complied with in that case. Their Lordship further decided that, this kind of termination enmasse is never contemplated in Regulation 52(2) of the BADC Service Regulation 1990. The impugned order itself shows non application of mind to the individual merit of the case of each of the individual petitioners before their service is terminated.

53. As against the said judgment, in Writ Petition No.6071 of2003 the BADC authority preferred Civil Appeal No.158-184 of 2006 which was heard along with Civil Appeal No.136 of 2007 which has been reported in 5 LG (AD) 256 and 60 DLR (AD) 152. In the said decision their Lordship in the Apex Court categorically came to the decisive decision in the following manner;

"It is true that the appellant should have the authority to terminate the employment of "undesirable" inefficient, corrupt, indolent and disobedient employees but such authority must be exercised fairly, objectively and independently and the occasion for the exercise must be delimited with precision and clarity" as was held in the case of Delhi Transport Corporation vs DTC Mazdoor Congress reported in AIR 1991 (SC) 101.

Apart from the aforesaid decision of the Apex Court their Lordship in the case of BJMC vs SAH Monower Ali reported in 5 LG (AD) 249 further indicates that the situation contemplates in the provision of termination simpliciter must be considered while ascertaining the legality and propriety of the exercise of power under such provision.

54. The aforesaid two decisions, of the apex Court, reported in 5 LG (AD) 256 and 5 LG (AD) 249 mandated this Court to take the apparent view that the power available under Provision of termination simpliciter, as in the case of Biman under the Service Regulation 52, may be exercised, but before such exercise the situation that contemplates in the provision must exist and that such authority must be exercised fairly, objectively,' independently and it must be exercised with precision which is to be taken into consideration that at the time of adjudicating whether such exercise was lawful.

55. But the learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam with due respect to the aforesaid decisions humbly argued that those decisions were made per incurriam as this was decided without considering or in ignorance of the series of decisions earlier passed by the Appellate Division on the similar point, and, as such, the instant decision is not a binding precedent. The learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam further argued that even these decisions, aforesaid, cannot be taken in the premises that these have impliedly ruled over and relied earlier decisions of the Appellate Division since the Appellate Division in the aforesaid cases did not at all consider the previous decisions of the said Court on the relevant point. In this respect Mr Imam relied on the passage from the Book "Constitutional Law of Bangladesh" by Mr Mahmudul Islam.

56. Paragraph No. 5.214 A of the book "Constitutional Law of Bangladesh" by Mr Mahmudul Islam contains the annotation on the subject under the heading "Overruling by implication." It contains as follows:

5.214: "Overruling by implication: Where the Appellate Division has applied its mind to the facts of the case before it and the law as declared by it in a previous case, the previous case shall be deemed to have been impliedly overruled if the law declared in the previous case contradicts what has been stated in the later case even though the previous case has not been expressly overruled.

57. In the light of the aforesaid annotation we have examined whether the earlier decisions of the apex Court were in any manner brought to the notice of the apex Court and this Court finds that in the case of Secretary BJMC vs SAH Monower Ali reported in 43 DLR (AD) 154 in the case of BST Corporation vs Mahbub Hossain reported in 29 DLR (SC) 41 were although referred by their Lordships in the body of judgments and in the impugned judgment of those cases passed by the High Court Division, the case of Bangladesh Bank vs Md Abdul Mannan reported in 46 DLR (AD) 1 and other decisions were relied upon by the respondents in substantiating their arguments that the termination simpliciter provision available in the Service Rules are valid law.

58. In the aforesaid cases reported in 29 DLR (SC) 41. the honorable Chief Justice, Mr Justice Syed AB Mahmud Hossain, after considering enormous decisions of home and aboard decided the case of dismissed employee of Bangladesh Small Industries Corporation and also of Janata Bank on the point of maintainability of writ petition against the statutory corporation and the application of the doctrine Audi alteram partem in case of termination simpliciter decisively found;

"Simple termination of service without giving a blame or stigma even though illegal, or irregular will not attract the operation of the principle of natural justice in such case."

59. In the case of Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation vs Shahid Hossain Bhuiyan reported in 43 DLR (AD) 154 the honourable Chief Justice, Mr Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed while considering the effect of termination simpliciter provision of Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation Service Rules, 1980, Rule 41 (2)(i)(ii) decides as follows;

"This provision for termination is undoubtedly a harsh provision, for even an officer/ employee having a long period of service to his credit may be determined just by 30 days' notice or by paying 30 days' salary in lieu thereof. Possibility of arbitrary exercise of this power to terminate is there. The pay in lieu of notice is also very negligible i.e., one month's pay. In many other organisations or industrial establishments, ordinarily three months' pay, along with gratuity at the rate of one months' for each completed year of service is allowed to a terminated employee. In such cases, an employee terminated cannot have any grievance; it is the payment of this and other service benefits which put a check upon arbitrary exercise of the power to terminate. But a Court cannot declare a law invalid on the ground that it is harsh or unjust. If the termination is found to be within the four corners of the law the Court cannot nullify it on the ground that it is harsh to cruel."

60. The aforesaid judgment reported in 43 DLR (AD) 154 was delivered on 8th August, 1990; three years later his Lordship the Chief Justice Mr Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed changed his view in the case of Bangladesh Bank vs Md Abdul Mannan and others and delivered the judgment on 12th July 1993 reported in 46 DLR (AD) 1 wherein his Lordship the honourable Chief Justice Mr Shahabuddin Ahmed held that "if the order of termination on the face of it does not entail any stigma or does not refer to any obligation, the termination in simpliciter" and further held as under;

"Before we leave we once against observe that though termination simpliciter of an employee of any statutory body may be permissible in law, such measure is very harsh and sometimes may cause injustice; the Rule providing for termination may be used in a discriminatory manner, in particular, to get rid of a conscientious employee who does not toe the line of his capricious boss. We. are fully aware of the fact that the main function of the Bangladesh Bank and for that purpose of any other statutory body or corporation is commercial in nature and their affairs are to be run from commercial point of view and for that purpose the procedure for removal of any undesirable employee should be free from any protracted proceeding, as applicable to a Government servant, But in the case of permanent employees of these bodies the length of service should be taken into consideration and for that purpose. service benefits such as gratuity according to the completed years of service may be given. Their service regulations may be amended so as to meet the ends of justice as well as the requirement of time.

61. Upon perusal of these decisions it appears that entire question relating to the termination simpliciter as available in various service rules of the statutory corporation have been brought to the notice of their Lordships in the apex Court and their Lordships upon full appraisal of the aforesaid earlier decisions of the apex Court decided the case reported in 5 LG (AD) 256 and 5 LG (AD) 249, upon applying their mind to the facts of the case before it and the law as declared by the Appellate Division in previous cases and therefore it can be safely noted that even the decisions in the earlier cases contradicts with the aforesaid cases and the. said previous cases were not expressly overruled, but by the later decisions the earlier decisions were overruled by implication. This Court notes that even the same honourable Chief Justice Mr Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed had a sharp turn in the case reported in 46 DLR (AD) 1 on the point of application of the provision of termination simpliciter against the permanent employees and took a different view, as underlined by us, without expressly overruling the earlier decisions reported in 43 DLR (AD) 154. The implication that may be deduced from the decisions reported in 46 DLR (AD) 1,5 LG (AD) 256 and 5 LG (AD) 249 is that the apex Court although did not overrule the earlier decisions but now have taken a changed stance against the termination simpliciter matter, applied against the permanent employees, having no reason for such application. Therefore this Court finds little substance in the arguments of the learned Senior Advocate Mr Akhter Imam that the decisions made in the case reported in 5 LG (AD) 249 and 5 LG (AD) 256 were passed per incuriam.

62. But as the learned Senior Advocate Mr Akhter Imam, appearing on behalf of Biman, vehemently assailed the instant Rules on the ground of maintainability and since that goes to the root of the cause, the same should be addressed earlier than to decide the merit of the case.

63. It has been contended by Mr Imam that these Rules have became infructuous due to the transformation of the employer, the national flag carrier, from its previous status of statutory corporation to a public limited company. According to him, a public limited company, not being amenable to the jurisdiction of Article 102 of the Constitution, these Rules cannot be maintained, on the ground that during the pendency of these Rules the employer Bangladesh Biman Corporation, against whom the writ petitioners obtained the Rules, has became a public limited company under the name and style Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited. Moreover, Mr Imam contends that even the 100% share of the public limited company of the Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited is owned by the government, yet the government having no supervisory authority upon the administration of Biman Bangladesh Air- lines Limited, a writ of mandamus cannot be issued against the Biman Bangladesh Airlines. Therefore, these Rules not only became infructuous but also not maintainable on the present context.

64. This Court is unable to concede to the argument of the learned Advocate Mr Akhter Imam. Because the power under Regulation 52 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation 1979 terminating the service of the writ petitioners has been exercised by the Bangladesh Biman Corporation in the month of May 2007, while the same was a statutory corporation. The writ petitioners obtained these Rules within the said month of May 2007. Thereafter, during the pendency of these Rules, the national flag carrier has been transformed into a public limited company. Therefore the cause as brought before this Court, had arisen at a point of time when the national flag carrier was a statutory corporation and it was decided in a series of decisions of this Court and the apex Court, that the writ petition is maintainable against the statutory corporation under the Provision of the Constitution. The transformation of the status of the statutory corporation, during the pendency of the Rules shall have no implication on the Rules and the same will not make the Rules infructuous. The word infructuous means making nullity by doing something which directly affects the circumstances under which the cause of action arose and by such doing the cause of action becomes nullity. This may be stated by the example that if during the pendency of these Rules the Biman authority reinstate the writ petitioners in their respective, post than only on that case, it could be argued that the Rules have became infructuous. The case brought against the national flag carrier, while it was in the status of Statutory Corporation, is the issue before this Court to be adjudicated and only the legality and propriety or the action involved in the case will be considered by this Court and any extraneous matter in respect of the change of status of the respondent shall have no implication on the Rules and therefore this Court finds that the Rules have not became infructuous.

65. So far the next ground against the maintainability of these Rules are concerned, the learned Advocate Mr Akhter Imam attempted to impress this Court that the 100% shares of the public limited company Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited although being held by the government, yet the company not being under the day to day or even supervisory authority of the government is not amenable to the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution. But this question has already been decided by series of decision of home and abroad in which the terms "public body" has been defined in the premises that when an authority exercises the power of the government as its instrumentality in any manner, that makes the authority a public body, amenable to the jurisdiction of judicial review of the superior Court.

66. In our jurisdiction this question was examined by a specially constituted larger Bench of the High Court Division in case of Mr Arif Sultan vs Chairman, Dhaka Electric Supply Authority Ltd reported in 2008 BLD (AD) 332 wherein the Special Division Bench, comprised by their Lordship Mr Justice Awlad Ali, Mr Justice ABM Khairul Hoque and Mr Justice Syed Mahmood Hossain, while examined the definition of such instrumentality of the government, came to the finding that so long the entire share of the new company is held by the government, it has all the dominion, functionally and administratively, over the company and such a state of affairs made the new company and instrumentality or agency of the government, but when the government has only a regulatory authority it would not serve to make a company an instrumentality of the government which means that if the authority has the supervisory overlooking from the government, still it could be treated as a concern of the government to act as state instrumentality and thereby a public body.

<u>67. The principle is equally applicable to the case of Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited as the 100% share of the public company is still owned by the Government of Bangladesh. The service rendering by the Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited is to be rendered by the Government of Bangladesh under its governmental duty to provide all the amenities of life, in which the air passage is also included and as the same is the primary responsibility of the government, it can be safely said that the Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited although a public limited company is a public body as it is a governmental instrumentality, amenable to the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution. Moreover, the Section 2 of the <u>Service (Re-organisation and Conditions) Act 1975 (Act No. XXXII of 1975)</u> has provided the same in the following language;</u>

<u>Service (Re-organisation and Conditions) Act 1975 (Act No. XXXII of 1975)</u>

<u>Section 2. Definitions-In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context.</u>

<u>(a) "Nationalised Enterprise" includes any industrial or commercial concern which is owned, controlled or managed by or vested in the government or any public body;</u>

<u>(b) "pay" includes salary, allowance and any other emoluments by whatever name called;</u>

<u>(c) "Public body" means any body, authority corporation or institution or constituted or established by or under any law and includes any other body authority or institution owned, controlled, managed or set up by the government;</u>

<u>(d) "Service includes any post or office.</u>

68. We have already found on a discussion on the referred case as made by the learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam that the earlier view of this Court including the Indian jurisdiction has been changed and expanded with a view to good governance of the public body in which it was decisively decided that even if power under provision of termination simpliciter is available to a public body, the same must be exercised only on the contemplated situation as provided in such provision and not otherwise, which did not allow the public body to exercise the same enmasse in order to get rid of the employees with a view to downsize their personnel department.

69. The learned Advocate Mr Akhter Imam since asked this Court to take into consideration the attempt of the government to make viable the national flag carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited a profitable concern for the interest of the nation, this Court notes that the interest of the terminated employees should also be considered in the light of the public policy. A welfare country like Bangladesh has the constitutional obligation to look after the good governance of every public body, specially in concerning the interest of the employees, through which good governance of the public body could be ensured and, as such, the welfare and well- being of the employees of public body culminates into public policy and any indiscriminate dealing with the interest of such employees of the public body affects the public policy as well.

<u>70. Under the service Regulations of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation, the writ petitioners were employed initially in the category of probationer against the permanent post which has been defined in Regulation 2(X) of the Service Regulation, 1979 as meaning a "Post so designated carrying a definite rate of pay and sanction without limit of time". Later the Writ petitioners, upon their successful completion of probation period were confirmed against their permanent post, under the provision of Regulation 10 of the Service Regulation 1979. What is the implication of permanency of service in the permanent post if the confirmed employee is amenable under Regulation 52 of the Service Regulation? This Court notes that the same makes that confirmation a nugatory one. Therefore, this Court finds that the situation that contemplated in the Regulation 52 of the Service Regulation, 1979, as their Lordships in the Apex Court has decided to be looked into in the case reported in 5 LG (AD) 256 at the time of ascertaining the legality and propriety of the exercise of power under Regulation 52, is to our considerate view that each and every individual case is to be considered on its own merit by the employer before exercising such power and, as such, the said power cannot be applied enmasse in achieving a goal to reduce the manpower of Biman.</u>

<u>71. It appears from materials on record, though denied by the Learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam, that this is a case of enmasse termination, this Court finds that in order to materialise the decision of the Board of Directors of the Biman Corporation, the writ petitioners were victim of termination enmasse along with total of 66 officers of the corporation and, as such, in view of decisions of the apex Court this Court has no hesitation but to hold that this termination of the writ petitioners enmasse through exercising power under Regulation 52 of the Service Regulation, 1979, was made without lawful authority.</u>

72. But the question, that has been raised by the learned Senior Counsel Mr Akhter Imam, whether the writ petitioners should be reinstated in their respective post or they should be allowed damage for the illegal termination of their employment prematurely, merits consideration.

73. It appears that the Biman is in lack of skilled employees and having found so, the Biman is now admittedly recruiting employees on contract basis paying a higher salary. The annexure, appended to the supplementary affidavit, as submitted by the petitioners, manifest that a considerable number of employees have been appointed under contract basis by the Biman, currently paying a higher pay. The learned Advocate Mr Imam vigorously denies that any such employees appointed on contractual basis, has been employed permanently, rather all the employees who have been appointed as such are casual employee on the daily payment basis on the requirement of the employer Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited. But the fallacy of the argument of the learned Advocate Mr Akhter Imam lies in the point that he does not deny the requirement of the employees by the Biman. However the requirement of employees either on the basis of contract or on the basis of recruitment Rules is the matter to be decided by the Biman to which this Court has nothing to say, but since the writ petitioners were illegally terminated from their job at the time when they were the employees of the statutory corporation, they will be entitled to be reinstated in their respective post since the national flag carrier, after its transformation to public limited company, has not lost its status as a public body. Therefore, this Court finds merit in these Rules and finds that the writ petitioners are entitled to be reinstated in their respective posts.

74. In the result the Rules are made absolute.

75. The impugned order of termination of the writ petitioners in exercise of power available under the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees Regulation 52 of the (Service) Regulation, 1979 are hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority.

76. The respondents are directed to reinstate the writ petitioners in their respective post with all back wages and benefit.

However, there shall be no order as to cost.

End.
