case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 7th day of May, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4274 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated the 7th day of May, 2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4274 of 2006 dis-charging the Rule.

2. Facts giving rise to this appeal are that respondent Nos. 1-14 as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 33 of 1997 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Begumgonj of the mortgage. Latter on the suit being transferred to the Court of the Assistant Judge, Companygonj was renumbered as Title Suit No. 135 of 2005.

3. The plaint case, in short, was that Momtaz Miah, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs, mortgaged 15 decimals land for rupees 1000 for a tenure of 5 years and 12 decimals land of rupees 80700 for a tenure of 4(four) years to Moniruddin, predecessor-in-interest of the defendants by two registered kabala being Nos. 1245 and 1248 dated the 11th day of February, 1966 and on the same date, Moniruddin executed and registered two agreements being Nos. 1247 and 1249 in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessor-Momtaz Miah agreeing that he would execute and register the deed of reconveyance to Momtaz Miah if the kabala money was repaid by him (Momtaz Miah) within the said stipulated period of the agreements. Thereafter, Momtaz Miah went to jail and on 07.02.1976, he repaid the kabala money by three installments to Moniruddin and on receiving the kabala money, he (Moniruddin) gave receipt and delivered possession of the suit land to Momtaz Miah. But, in the meantime, Moniruddin became seriously ill for which he was unable to execute and register the deed of reconveyance. Thereafter, Moniruddin filed a title suit in the Court of Munsif, Third Court, Noakhali for permanent injunction against Momtaz Miah and got a decree and on the strength of that decree, the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land. On the death of Momtaz his heirs filed title appeal before the Court of District Judge, Noakhali against the judgment and decree of the trial Court which was dismissed. As the impugned transaction were made with condition to reconvey, on the expiry of 7 years, the plaintiffs were entitled to redemption of the suit land; hence, they instituted the suit for the relief aforementioned.

4. Defendant Nos. 1-5 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable. Momtaz Miah, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs, sold (12+15)=27 decimals land, i.e. the suit land to Moniruddin, predecessor-in-interest of the defendants for rupees 807.00 and for rupees 1000 respectively by two registered kabalas dated the 11th day of February, 1966 and Moniruddin agreed to reconvey the said respective quantum of lands if Momtaz Miah could repay the money by Magh 1373 B.S. and by Magh 1377 B.S. and accordingly, he executed and registered two agreements in that respect. It was also agreed that if the vendor-Momtaz Miah failed to return the kabala money within the prescribed period, the respective transaction became out and out sale after the stipulated period. As Momtaz Miah and his people threatened to dispossess Moniruddin from the suit land, he (Moniruddin) filed Title Suit No. 90 of 1979 in the Court of Munsif, Third Court, for permanent injunction which was decreed on contest on 31.08.1995. Against the Judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.90 of 1979, Momtaz Miah filed Title Appeal No. 187 of 1985 before the District Judge, Noakhali which was dismissed on contest on 7th October, 1985. Tenure of reconveyance expired long before the promulgation of the Presidential Orders were not applicable in the present case. The defendants as the heirs of Moniruddin have been possessing the suit land by exercising their absolute right and title therein. The plaintiffs were not entitled to get redemption of the suit land as it was not a mortgage and that it was not redeemed in time as per the agreement in time as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed.

5. At the trial, 3 (three) PWs and 2(two) DWs Were examined and the documents were filed by the respective party which were proved and marked as exhibits in support of their respective case.

6. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 27.09.2005 dismissed the suit on the finding, inter alia, that the transactions became past and closed long before the insertion of section 95A in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950) and as such, the said section had no manner of application; the plaintiffs failed to prove that their predecessor-in-interest paid back the kabala money and got back possession of the suit land that subsequently, they were dispossessed by the defendants; since the plaintiffs claimed that in payment of the kabala money by their predecessor-in-interest, he got back possession of the suit land, but subsequently, Moniruddin did not execute and register the deed of reconveyance, the suit for redemption was not maintainable and the plaintiffs ought to have filed the suit for specific performance of contact.

7. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 222 of 2005 before the District Judge, Noakhali. The learned Joint District Judge, Third Court, Noakhali having heard the appeal, by his judgment and decree dated 28.08.2006 allowed the same, set aside the judgment and decree dated 28.08.2006 allowed the same, set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 28.08.2006. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the defendants filed the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division. A learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1167 of 2009 before this Court and leave was granted to consider the grounds as under:

"the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering that Safkabalas and agreements to reconvey dated 11.02.1966 and tenure of agreement relating to Safkabala No. 1246 was 4 years and tenure of another agreement relating to Safkabala No. 1247 was 5 years and the tenure of the agreement expired on 11.02.1970 and 11.02.1971 respectively long before President's Order No. 88 of 1972 inserting Section 95A to the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was inserted which was made on 03.08.1972 and as such transactions relating to the suit land was past and closed at the time of making of P.O. 88 of 1972 and as such it did not hit the transaction relating to the suit land in view of the law laid down in the cases reported in 1 BLC(AD) 164, 32 DLR (AD) 233, 1 DCC(AD) 60, 33 DLR(AD) 233 and 2008 (XVI) BLT (AD) 357 and therefore the Judgment and Order passed by the High Court Division are not sustainable in law" and "Regard being had to the fact that in order to attract Section 58(e) (sic, it would be 58(c)) of Transfer of Property Act to a transaction the condition is to be embodied in the sale deed but in the present case no such condition of redemption was contained in the sale deed as such the present transaction is an out and out sale and it cannot be treated as mortgage and the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in discharging the Rule without considering this aspect of the case and therefore, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division are not sustainable in law."

8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel for the appellants, in fact, has made his submissions elaborating the grounds on which leave was granted. Therefore, we need not restate his submissions as that would be absolutely nothing but repetition.

9. Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam, learned Advocate for respondent Nos. 1-14, has supported the impugned judgment and order. In support of his submission, he referred the case of Asmatunnessa and others-Vs-Tenu Khan and another, (1992) 12 BLD (AD) 216.

10. From the facts as emerged from the pleadings of the respective party, it appears that it is an admitted fact that the agreements for reconveyance of the lands of the two kabalas were executed on the same date of the kabalas, i.e. on 11.02.1996 fixing the tenure to repay the kabala money within 4(four) years in respect of kabala No. 1246 and 5 (five) years in respect of kabala No. 1247 and the tenure for repayment of the kabala money in respect of those kabalas expired on 11.02.1971 and 11.02,1972 respectively, i.e. ling before the insertion of section 95A in the Act, 1950 on 03.08.1972 by P.O. 88 of 1972 and the transactions relating to the suit land became past and closed. Therefore, the plaintiffs had no subsisting rights to pray for redemption of the mortgage as prayed for in the suit. This Court in the case of Bangladesh -Vs- Haji Abdul Gani Biswas and others, 32DLR (AD) 233; Abdul Khaleque Sarnamat-Vs-Abdul Khaleque Sarnamat and another, 1BLC(AD)90; Abu Bakkar-Vs-Nazir Ahmed, 34 DLR(AD)237 and Mahadeb Chandra Mondol and another-Vs-Dulal Chandra Mondal and others 16 BLT(AD) (2008) 357 clearly held so but the Appellate Court as well as the High Court Division totally misconceived the provisions of section 95A of the Act, 1950 vis-a-vis the facts and circumstances of the case and also failed to apply their mind to the principles of law enunciated by this Court in the above mentioned reported cases in holding that the transactions in question were not hit by the principle of past and closed transactions and thereby fell into an error in decreeing the suit.

<u>11. Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam very much relied upon the observation made by this Court in the case of Asmatunnessa and others (supra) to the effect "It may be observed that the learned Judge completely failed to appreciate the provisions of Section 95A of the S.A.T. Act. The Section clearly envisages that a transfer of a holding etc by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding etc. for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the documents relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years to strengthen his submission that the view of the agreement of reconveyance the transactions in question were complete usufructuary mortgage, so after the expiry of 7(seven) years, the plaintiffs were entitled to redeem the same in view of the provisions of section 95A of the Act." The quoted observations made by this Court in the above cited case do not help Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam inasmuch as in the reported case, the registered deed and the Ekrarnama, it was stipulated that the land would be reconveyed if the kabala. money amounting to taka 400.00 (four hundred) was returned within four years and this four years would end on 22.10.1974, whereas section 95A was inserted in Act, 1950 by P.0.88 of 1972 on 03.08.1972, so by no stretch of imagination, it could be said that the transaction involved in the reported case (Asmatunnessa and others) became a past and closed one before the insertion of section 95A in the Act. Moreso, in the reported case, the question of past and closed transaction was not at all raised and decided. It also needs to be mentioned that in the reported case, this Court also observed that "the facts of the instant case fully answer the above description and it is clear that the transaction thus qualified to be a complete usufructuary mortgage by operation of law."</u>

12. But in the instant case as discussed above, the facts do not answer the description of the respective transaction to be a complete usufructuary mortgage.

13. Besides, the above legal aspect of the case, the plaintiffs also failed to prove their case factually. In the plaint, it was asserted that their predecessor-in-interest, Momtaz Miah, paid back the kabala money to the defendants' predecessor-in-interest, Moniruddin as per terms of the agreement and then he got back possession of the suit land and thereafter, he was disposed. The trial Court gave clear finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove that their predecessor-in-interest paid back the kabala money to Moniruddin and that he got back possession of the suit land.

<u>14. The trial Court also held that as per the own case of the plaintiffs, the mortgage was redeemed with the return of the kabala money followed by delivery of possession of the suit land, but subsequently, Moniruddin did not execute and register the deed of reconveyance, if that be so, the plaintiffs could not have any cause of action to main the suit for redemption of the suit land and that they ought to have filed a suit for redemption of the suit land and that they ought to have filed a suit for specific performance of contract. We have considered the evidence. The trial Court was perfectly correct in taking the said factual and legal view. But neither the Appellate Court nor the High Court Division adverted the above findings of the trial Court in decreeing the suit.</u>

15. For the discussions made above, we find merit in the appeal and the same is allowed. The impugned judgment and order affirming those of the Appellate Court is set aside and those of the trial Court are restored. There will be no order as to cost.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J : At the instance of the petitioners Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned letter contained in Memo No, শিম/শাঃ/৫-বি-6/2005/244 dated 4-6-2009 (Annexure A) issued by respondents No.6 and impugned letter dated 13-4-2009 (AnnexureA-1 ) should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to the this court may seen fit and proper.

2. The relevant facts which are required for disposal of the writ petition are that on 13-4-2009 the respondent No. 5 issued a letter under Memo No. অম/অবি(বাস্ত-২)/বেতন বৈষম্য/শিক্ষা-১/২০০৯/৭৬ তারিখ ১৩/৪/২০০৯ ইং to the secretary Ministry of Education informing that it was not possible to upgrade the scale of Superintendent and Auditor. After receiving the letter dated 13-4-2009 the Respondent No.6 issued another letter dated 11-6-2009 under Memo শিম/শাঃ/৫-বি-৬/২০০৫/২৪৪ তাং ১১-৬-২০০৯ containing the reference of the respondent No. 5 's decision to refuse up gradation and the petitioners received on 16-6-2009. The petitioner impugned the said letters challenging the illegality and seeking direction upon the respondents to upgrade the scale of the petitioner No. 1 in the scale of Taka 5100-10360 and for the petitioner No. 2 in the scale of Taka 4,100-8820.

3. It is stated that the petitioner No. 1 Abdus Samad Miah was appointed on 17-9-1974 as LD Clerk and joined in the service on 20-9-1974 in the same post under the Ministry of Education. On 20-9-1981 he was promoted to the Post of UD and Joined on 30-4-1981, and on 18-2-85 he was promoted to the post of Auditor. Thereafter he was promoted the post of Superintendent by an order dated 11-12-1989 and joined to the post on the same date. Now he is serving as Superintendent in the office of Directorate of Inspection and Audit, Ministry of Education, Shikkha Bhaban, Dhaka. The petitioner No. 2 Md Momtazul Karim was appointed on 28- 10-1970 as LD Clerk and joined in service on 4-11-1970 in the same post under the Ministry of Education and on 21-12-1981 he was promoted to the post of UD and joined there on 29-11-1981. Thereafter on 18-2-1985 he was promoted to the post of Auditor. Now he is serving as Auditor in the office of the Directorate of Inspection and Audit, Ministry of Education, Shikkha Bhaban, Dhaka.

4. It is also stated that on 20-8-1998, the Deputy Secretary-1 (Bastobayon), Ministry of Finance, issued a notification under Memo No. অস/অবি (বাস্ত)-১/অডিটরউঃ স্কেল-৪/৯৭/১৫৯ to upgrade the scale of Auditor (AG) from Taka 2250-4735 to 2550-5505. The notification was issued by the order of the President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Pursuant to the above notification while the scale of the Auditor (AG) Ministry of Finance was increased. The petitioner No.1 submitted an application on 16-9-1998 to the respondent No. 3 for up gradation of their scale and to bring equality with the scale of Auditor of (AG). The Ministry of Finance. The said application contained that the education qualification and status of both the posts are same but the scale of the Auditor (AG), Ministry of Finance, has been upgraded by the said Notification in which the post of the petitioner No. 1 was mentioned.

5. It was requested by the petitioners to take steps for bringing equality with the scale of the Auditory (AG), Ministry of Finance and the Scale of the petitioner No.1. The petitioner No.2 also submitted an application of 15-7-2000 to the respondent No. 3 for up gradation his scale. It was mentioned that, who are serving as Superintendent (AG). Ministry of Finance, they are getting salary at Taka 3400-6625 but serving in equivalent post as Superintendent, Ministry of Education, the petitioner, is getting less salary, which is discriminatory.

6. On 9-11-2005 the senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Education sent a letter to the Secretary, Ministry of Finance and requested to take steps for upgradation of the scale of the petitioners. Thereafter on 6-4-2008 the Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Education sent a proposal through a letter under Memo No. শিম/শাঃ/৫-বি-৬/২০০৫/১২৮ to the Secretary, Ministry of Finance. It was stated in the letter that the scale of the two posts of the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Education were in same service and performing same job.

7. It was stated that in the summary of the Ministry of Finance it is shown that the scale of the petitioners was similar with the scale of the Auditor (AG) Ministry of Finance. As per national scale of 1977, 1985, 1991 and 1997 both the posts of Auditor Ministry of Education and Ministry of Finance were getting the same scale. On 9-7-2008 the petitioner No. 2 submitted an application to the respondent No. 3 in which prayer was made to take steps to remove discrimination about the scale of the petitioners with others. The Director, Directorate of Audit and Inspection, Ministry of Education, wrote a letter on 15-7-2008 to the Secretary, Ministry of Education requesting the discrimination between the Ministries and with the other departments should be removed.

8. Moreover it was also mentioned that others department took steps for removing the discrimination. On 13-10-2008 the Ministry of Finance sent a letter to the Secretary, Ministry of Education and asked to submit some papers and on 24-11-2008 the Director Directorate of Audit and Inspection, wrote a letter to the Secretary, Ministry of Education in which detailed statement was made and requested to fix the scale for the petitioner No. 1 at Taka 5100-10360 and for the petitioner No. 2 at Taka 4100-8820.

9. On 13-4-2009 the respondent No.5 issued a letter under Memo No. অস/অবি(বাস্ত-২) বেতন বৈষম্য/শিক্ষা-১/২০০৯/৭৬তারিখ ১৩-৪-২০০৯ ইং to Secretary, Ministry of Education. It was informed by the letter that it was not possible to upgrade the scale of Superintendent and Auditor. After receiving the letter dated 13-4-2009 the Respondent No. 6 issued another letter 11-6-2009 under Memo No. সিম/শাঃ৫/৫ বি-৬/২০০৫/২৪৪ and the petitioner receive on 16-6-2009. The petitioners impugned this letter challenging the illegality and seeking direction upon the respondents to upgrade the scale of the petitioner No. 1 having made all efforts to get their scale upgraded but failed, thus the petitioners invoked this writ Jurisdiction and obtained this rule

10. Mr. Manizil Murshed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are working in the post of Superintendent is equivalent to the post of Auditor (AG) Superintendent (AG) Ministry of Finance, but scale of the Auditor and Superintendent in the Ministry of Finance was upgraded by the notification dated 208-1998 issued by Ministry of Finance. Whereas the petitioners scales as Auditor and Superintendent have not been upgraded from Taka 2250-4735 to Taka 2550-5505 even though it is equal to the Auditor and Superintendent in the Ministry of Finance which is discriminatory and violative to provision of Constitution and therefore illegal and without lawful authority

11. The learned Advocate also submitted that the petitioners are working and performing the duties of the post successfully therefore they are entitled to get equal scale of the Auditor and Superintendent (AG) under the Ministry of Finance. Hence the petitioners scale should be upgraded but by refusing to upgrade the respondents have been discriminatory and violative to the provisions of equality before law and equal protection of law.

12. He also submitted that even the petitioners are serving as the servants for the republic they are challenging discrimination and equality before law under Article 102 by way of filing a writ petition and the petitioners do not have to go to the Administrative Tribunal to pursue their right under the provision of Article 117 of the Constitution containing provisions for Administrative Tribunal to deal with the terms of condition of service in the Republic. In support of his argument learned Advocate for the petitioner cited decision reported in the Bangladesh vs Shamsul Haque reported in 12 MLR (AD) 25 = 59 DLR (AD) 54 where the Hon'ble Appellate Division held that refusal of the prayer of the respondent regarding the status and privilege by the impugned orders passed by the Ministry of Finance for the writ petitioner as Typist Cum LDA serving in the Supreme Court of Bangladesh a writ petition is maintainable. Their Lordships held that writ petitioner had right to come in the High Court Division

13. The learned Advocate also refers to a case of Sazedur Rahman vs Secretary Ministry of Establishment reported in 50 DLR 407 in which this Court decided that even in the presence of the alternative remedy the petitioner instead of the going to the Administrative Tribunal can come before this Court for the protection of fundamental right and equal opportunity of the service in Republic of Bangladesh. However, in the above case their Lordships Mr. Justice KM Hasan and Mr. Justice Tafazzal Islam was pleased to hold that the law stands the proper forum for the petitioner (in writ petition No.3726/1997) is the Administrative Tribunal as the virus of law has not been challenged in the instant case but only in the matter of the fundamental rights challenging by a writ petition was maintainable and the rule Will issued

14. Pursuant to the above facts and the arguments thereof, the learned Advocate for the petitioner finally submitted that petitioners have been discriminated in their service and the petitioners are entitled to equal protection of law, he therefore prayed to make the rule absolute.

15. The rule has been vehemently opposed by the respondent No. 2 and filed an Affidavit-in-Opposition controverting the statements made in the writ petition. It is stated that up gradation of pay scale of Auditor and Superintendents of the Ministries/Division were made after recommendation of the cabinet committee and the Advisory committee for fixation of pay scale which was approved by the then Prime Minister. The Ministry of Education put forward a proposal for upgradation of pay scale of the petitioners by comparing with the upgraded pay scale of Auditor and Superintendent of CGA office, internal Audit Department under the Ministry of Housing and public works and under the Ministry of Foods. The Ministry of Finance issued Memo No. অস/অবি(বাস্ত-২)/বেতন বৈষম্য/শিক্ষা-১-২০০৯-৭৮" dated 13-4-2009 rejecting their claim as being not local and lawful. The pay scale of Auditor and Superintendent Ministry of Land was upgraded as per the order of the Administrative Tribunal through the case Nos. 90/2004, 91/2004. The pay scale of those posts in the Ministry of Land were not upgraded by a normal course of the Ministry of Finance and petitioners claim for upgradation of pay scale was not the same ground thus their prayer for upgradation was rejected. It is further stated that the post of Audit and Superintendent are common posts bearing almost common Categories of pay scale in all offices. It is further submitted that the petitioners are working in the post of Superintendent and Auditor, Which are equivalent to the post of Auditor (AG), and Superintendent (AG) Ministry of Finance but the scale of the petitioners are not same than the scale of Auditor and Superintendent (AG). The scale of the Auditor (AG), Ministry of Finance, was upgraded from Taka 2250-4735 to Taka 2550-5505 by the Ministry of Finance because they are serving in their Ministry.

16. It is also stated that the claim to upgrade the pay scale of petitioners was not similar to the cases of those Auditor and Superintendent of the Ministry of Finance. It is also stated that the claim by filing a writ petition is not justified and not maintainable because as being the employees under Republic there are other available forum under the existing law as provided under Article 117 of the Constitution and the petitioners can ventilate their grievances, as such, the writ petition is not maintainable under provision of Article 102 of the Constitution. It is also stated that petitioner claim for up gradation of scale is not a fundamental right but it is a subject matter of terms and conditions of service in the Republic including up gradation or fixation of pay scale.

17. Mr. M Khurshed Alam Sarker, the learned Deputy Attorney-General along with Mr. Abu Saleh Md Fazle Rabbi Khan, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the respondent No.2 submitted that the petitioners challenged the impugned orders dated 13-4-2009 and 11-6-2009 passed by respondents refusing to upgrade pay scale for the petitioner as being the Auditor and Superintendent in the Ministry of Education involves terms and conditions of service under the Service of the Republic.

18. For which an appropriate forum has been provided under Article 117 of the Constitution of Bangladesh. He also submitted that the forum or Administrative Tribunal is appropriate forum as the petitioners claim for up gradation of scale can be challenged in the Administrative Tribunal which being the appropriate applicable remedy. As such he submitted that the writ petition should be discharged as being not maintainable. The learned Deputy Attorney-General also submitted that the petitioners have right to upgrade the pay scale is a service right rather that to be considered as fundamental right because such a right comes within the ambit or the terms and conditions of the recruitment policy and the Government financial policy adopted in the service under the Republic. He therefore, pays to discharge the rule.

19. Having considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners and the respondent No.2 and also perusing the writ petition itself and Annexures therein and the affidavit-in-opposition and the Annexure thereof, we consider that the writ petitioners invoked this writ Jurisdiction by impugning a letter dated 13-4-2009 passed by the respondent No.5 and also a letter dated 11-6-2009 (Annexure-A) issued by the respondent No.6 refusing to upgrade the pay scale of the petitioners as being the Superintendent and Auditor serving under the Ministry of Education. The petitioner's main ground is that the petitioner have been discriminated because by a notification dated 20-8-1998 issued by the Ministry of Finance, the pay scale of Auditor (A G) was upgraded where as the petitioners are working and performing the same duties but the petitioners' application to up-grade pay scale was refused upgrade issued by Ministry of Finance.

20. From the above discussions it is apparent that the petitioners have been serving as an Auditor and a Superintendent under the Ministry of Education and any claim of up gradation of pay scale involves terms and conditions of service, we therefore consider that the petitioners can ventilate their grievance under the provision of Article 117 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, containing provision for remedies to be perused in the Administrative Tribunal. Regarding the maintainability of the writ petition the learned Advocate for the petitioners submitted before us that our apex Court in the Bangladesh vs Md Shamsul Haqueas referred in 12 MLR (AD) 2007 25 = 59 DLR (AD) 54 wherein their Lordship of the Hon'ble Appellate Division hold that the refusal of the prayer regarding the status and privilege of the petitioner as being in service in the

Republic a writ petition should be maintainable.

21. Having perused the said judgment we found that the circumstances are not similar to the present writ petition. Their Lordships were pleased to hold that a writ petition is maintainable when the Typist cum LDA serving in the Supreme Court of Bangladesh challenged refusal to upgrade similar salary and facilities with that of the employee's service of the Ministry. The present petitioners are not in the same footing as that of petitioners referred in 12 MLR (AD) 25 = 59 DLR (AD) 54 as the petitioners are in service under the Ministry of Education which is absolutely a Government Service. Therefore the petitioners are not entitled to get benefit of the decision referred to 12 MLR (AD) 2007.

22. The learned counsel for the petitioner also submitted that the petitioners were discriminated as the Auditor and Superintendent by the Ministry of Finance because the petitioners are in similar footing of the Auditor/Superintendent serving under the Ministry of Education but their pay scale has not been upgraded. Therefore it is a clear discrimination of the service of Republic. In this regard he drawn our attention to the reported case in 12 MLR (AD) 2007 25 = 59 DLR (AD) 54 wherein their Lordship hold that in case of discrimination in service of Republic an employee can invoke writ Jurisdiction. Here again we consider that it is a discrimination between service in the Supreme Court of Bangladesh and service of the Ministries. The writ petitioner in the case referred in 12 MLR (AD) 25 = 59 DLR (AD) 54 is not in the same footing as in the Ministry. As such we also consider that the petitioners' claim for discrimination does not stand similarly to discrimination between the employees of the Ministry of Finance and the employees of Supreme Court of Bangladesh. Therefore, the petitioners in this writ petition cannot get the benefit from the findings of their Lordship reported in 12 MLR (AD) 25 =59 DLR (AD) 54. We also consider that the decision of our apex Court in Mozibur Rahman vs Bangladesh referred in 44 DLR (AD) 111 is still a good law for a person in the service of Republic which strongly observed as follows:

" 46. Appellant in Civil Appeal No. 35 of 1987 contended that when he challenged the impugned order of compulsory retirement on the ground of violation of fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 27 and 29 of the Constitution the High Court Division ought to have exercised its jurisdiction under clause (1) of Article 102. It appears that no case of violation of any fundamental right was made out before the High Court Division nor any certificate was given in this regard. In Serajul Islam vs The Director General of Food, 42 DLR (AD) 199 this Court, in rejection the petitioner's contention that the Tribunal had no jurisdiction to give necessary relief when the fundamental right against a. double jeopardy was invoked, observed.

" We do not think so, for, if the petitioner can establish a case of double jeopardy on facts he can invoke the law under which he is proceeded against which cannot be opposed to fundamental rights and the Tribunal is competent to enforce the statue. The matter arising from a departmental proceeding relating to terms and conditions of service of the petitioner the High Court Division rightly found a bar to its jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution.

"47. The learned Additional Attorney- General.

48. Within its jurisdiction the Tribunal can strike down an order for violation of principles of natural justice as well as for infringement of fundamental rights, guaranteed by the Constitution, or of any other law, in respect of matters relating to or arising of sub-clause (a), but such tribunals cannot, like the India Administrative Tribunals in exercise of a more comprehensive jurisdiction under Article 323A (see SP Sampath Kumar vs Union of India. AIR 1937 SC 386 (Para 16) and JB Chopra vs Union of India AIR 1987 SC 357 (Para 2), strike down any law or rule on the ground of its Constitutionality. A person in the service of the Republic who intends to invoke fundamental right for challenging the vires of a law seek his remedy under Article 117(2)".

<u>23. From the finding of our Apex Court as above, we can hold that the remedies under Article 102 and under Article 117 of the Constitution are available for different contexts of rights. The persons who are employees under the service of the Republic enter in to service with specific terms and conditions of their service which do not come under the remedies available under Article 102 of the Constitution, subject to certain exceptions, because available efficacious remedy under Article 117 of the Constitutions. As such, the present petitioners as being the employees under the Ministry of Education cannot invoke writ Jurisdiction, in relation to upgradation of their pay scale.</u>

In view of the above discussion we are of the view that writ petition is not maintainable.

In the result, the rule is discharged with no order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Sharifuddin Chaklader J : This appeal by the plaintiffs Bank directed against the judgment dated 26-1-1997 and decree dated 22-1-1997 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Kushtia in Artha Rin Suit No. 131 of 1993 decreeing the suit without interest pendente lite.

2. The questions arisen for consideration :

(i) whether the Court is empowered to refuse interest pendent lite while decreeing the suit.

(ii) whether in a suit filed under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, Government recommendation for exemption of payment of interest pendent lite is applicable or not.

3. The plaintiff initiated the suit for realization of Taka 21,86,194with following prayers:

“(ক) বাদী ব্যাংক বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে গত ৩১-৭-৯৩ ইং তাং হিসাবে টাকা ২১,৮৬,১৯৪ (একুশ লক্ষ ছিয়াছি হাজার এক শত চুরানব্বই) টাকা আদায় বাবদ ব্যক্তিগত ডিক্রী পান।

(খ) মোকদ্দমার যাবতীয় খরচা বাবদ ডিক্রী পান।

(গ) অন্তরবর্তীকালীন চলামান সুদ ও সুদ আদায় বাবদ ডিক্রী পান।”

4. The fact of the case, although are not so much relevant for disposal of this appeal, but for a reference, it appears that defendants was sanctioned loan of Taka 15,00,000 + 2,00,000 = total 17,00,000 on 8-7-1989. Defendant defaulted in paying the loan and it pile up to Taka 21,86,194 and after request, when defendant did not pay the said amount or did not take any step for repaying the loan, that suit was filed. The defendant filed written statement and denied the facts of the plaintiff's case. The suit was decreed.

5. Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed, learned Advocate, submits that the Court has power to allow interest while decreeing the suit. Learned Advocate, relied on some of the decisions of the Appellate Division as well as High Court Division and submits that learned Judge acted illegally in not allowing interest while decreeing the suit.

6. Mr. Shasti Sarker, learned Advocate, appearing for the respondent, submits that the Court had power not to allow interest as the learned Judge fully relief on the recommendation of the Government for re-establishing the sick industries. The learned Advocate further submits that the recommendation made by the Government has far reaching effect and this judgment in fact will help the sick industries to survive as such, this judgment should not be set aside.

7. Learned Advocate for the respondent relied on the case of Sonali Bank vs Quaderia Publications and Products Limited. 17 BLT (AD) 148 where it has been held:-

" The High Court Division of hearing both sides made the rule absolute on the ground that the respondents had acquired a vested right on the basis of the Bangladesh Bank memo and the petitioner was stopped from denying the exemption of waiver of interest as proposed in the said memo. The High Court Division further directed the petitioner to allow the respondents waiver of 75% interest. It further came to the conclusion that allowing 40% exemption ignoring the recommendation of waiver of 75% by Bangladesh Bank, the controlling authority was unreasonable and arbitrary. It also came to the finding that the impugned order was discriminatory as other companies standing on the same footing with the petitioner has been allowed waiver from 70%-90%. Whereas the petitioner was victimized on political ground"

8. The learned Advocate for the respondent next relied on the case of Sonali Bank vs Messrs Beg and Beg Jute Incorporated Ltd, 17 BLD (AD) 313 = 2 BLC (AD) 173. wherein it has been held that:

"It thus appears that the pre-ponderance of judicial decisions In the sub-continent is that whether it is a suit for foreclosure or for sale the Court has to pass a preliminary decree in terms of Rule 2(1) of Order XXXIV and that the Court has no option but to award interest pendente to the mortgagee. In a suit for redemption the principle is not very different because the preliminary decree therein has to be passed under Order XXXIV Rule 7 CPC which is substantially in the same terms as in Rule 2. The High Court Division was not well-founded in law in not being persuaded with the decisions cited in AIR 1953 (Born) 445 and AIR 1958 (Rajasthan) 145 on the ground that as those were suits for foreclosure and redemption. The principles stated therein are inapplicable in the instant suit. In a suit for sale the preliminary decree is drawn up in the same manner as to a suit for foreclosure."

9. We, therefore, hold that the High Court Division acted illegally in not holding that the plaintiff appellant was entitled to interest pendente lite i.e. from the date of the institution of the suit upto the date of the passing of the decree.

10. Next decision the learned Advocate relied on case of Messrs MM Ispahani vs Sonali Bank. 37 DLR (AD) 1. Where in "Sonali Bank sanctioned Taka 3,49,14,734,70 for realization of the suit money plaintiff initiated Money Suit No. 172 of 1974. The suit was decreed. Thereafter, First Appeal No. 27 of 1981 was preferred before the High Court Division. The appeal was dismissed. The High Court Division on relying on the case of Maridas Ramchordas vs Mercantile Bank of India Ltd. 47 ILR (Bom)  where it has been held that the rate of interest which was charged by the Bank applicable as the objection was raised by the appellant and as it was duly shown in the statements of accounts on the basis of which entries were made therein. As to the rate of interest from the date of the filing of the suit to the date of judgment, the High Court Division held that as the award to interest fell within the discretion of the Court which was duly exercised by it, no interference was called for. The order of interest at the rate of 12% during the pendency of the suit and until realization did not suffer from any illegality."

11. It appears that all the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the respondent are on general law, not on special law like Artha Rin Adalat Ain. 2003.

12. On this point our High Court Division unanimous in its decision as Government recommendation merely been a recommendation having no force of law, is not applicable. Let us go through the cases decided by our Supreme Court on this point.

13. (i) In the case of Professor A Rahim Khan vs Bangladesh, 7 BLT (AD) 313, it has been held:

"It is true that the High Court Division suffered from a misconception of fact that there was already an agreement/contract between the parties and a dispute has arisen over the terms and conditions thereof which was the subject matter of the writ petition. In fact, the petitioners, came to the writ petition for a direction upon the respondents to finalize the agreement only on the basis of the recommendation of the Cabinet Committee as approved by the Prime Minister vide aforesaid Memo dated 8-5-94. The High Court Divisions misconception was there but the misconceived nature of the petitioner's writ petition was equally showing. Unfortunately, the High Court Division failed to take notice of the same and proceeded upon a wrong ground of fact. The recommendation of a Cabinet Committee cannot be enforced through a writ for the simple reason that it is not law. It is as simple as that. The Writ Petition was misconceived at the inception."

(ii) Messrs Greenways Tannery represented by its Proprietor Sirajuddin vs Secretary, Ministry of Industries, Government of Bangladesh. This Writ Petition No. 6270 of 2003 was filed for implementation of the recommendations made by Sick Industry Rehabilitation Cell in its report 25-8-92 and the rule of this writ petition was discharged by judgment dated 18-5-2004 by this Division.

(iii) Greenways Tannery and other vs Subordinate judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka. This Writ Petition No. 3292 of 1999 was filed challenging the institution and proceeding of Artha Rin suit on the ground that recommendations were not implemented by the Government and suit cannot be proceeded without implantations thereof. In this Writ Petition this Division by Judgment dated 18-5- 2004 decided as under :-

In the notification issued by the Government for implementation of the recommendation made by the, Government there is no legal obligation on the part of the loan granting bank not to initiate the legal proceeding or to institute a suit for realization of the outstanding dues and the recommendation and the policy as formulated in the notification dated 6-3-97 for settlement of the dues out of Court for the purpose of rehabilitation of the sick industries are not binding upon the respondent. bank and respondent will proceed for realization of the dues under the law, namely, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990."

(iv) Mirzaboo Steels Limited vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 59 DLR 141. This Writ Petition No. 1527 of 2001 was field for implementation of the recommendation of the Sick Industry Rehabilitation Cell dated 29-9-92. This Rule was discharged by this Division by judgment dated 13-12-2006 with the following observations:-

"However, it is now a settled principle of law that Article 102 of the Constitution can be invoked only where the petitioners right has undisputedly accrued under the Constitution or under any other legal instrument and such right has not been given effect to. In other words, the petitioner is being deprived of the benefit of such right. The aforesaid letter dated 29-9- 1992, Annexure B to the writ petition is not a legal instrument creating legal right for the petitioner for waiver of 100% interest and other benefits as has been observed above. It only lays down the policy of the government making recommendation for waiver of such interest without creating any legal right."

In view of the observations made above as to the enforce ability of the notification we are of the opinion that the notification dated 29-9-92, Annexure B to the writ petition has no force of law and accordingly has no binding effect upon the Respondent Bank. Moreover, the Legislature having had incorporated the same concept of amicable settlement in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the respective petitioner company cannot be said to have been left out without any forum to place its grievance in accordance with law. Hence, the proceeding of the Mortgage Suit being No. 71 of 1995 cannot be adjourned in view of Annexure-E and shall proceed in accordance with law. Considering the observations and the findings made hereinabove by this Court we are of the view that this Rule bears no merit for consideration. Accordingly, it is liable to be discharged.

(v) Edruk Ltd. vs Secretary, Ministry of Industries. This Writ Petition No. 7300 of2003 was also filed for direction for implementation of the recommendations made by the Sick Industry Rehabilitation Cell in its report dated 25-9-92. This Rule was also discharged by Judgment dated 1-10- 2007 deciding that the recommendation bears no binding force to the Court in any way.

(vi) In the case of Janata Bank vs Md Ibrahim Khalil, First Appeal No. 422 of 1998, a Division Bench of this Court, by judgment dated 9-3-2008, where similar question was raised i.e. whether Court can waive interest on the basis of the recommendation of the Government, hold that Government or the Court is not empowered or have any authority to waive interest charged on the amount under claim as per agreement executed. between the judgment debtor and the financial institution i.e. the plaintiff- Bank till its realization. The contemplation of the aforesaid provision of law is clear and unambiguous that the Court cannot waive such interest and it is the Bank itself who could waive such interest to whom the defendant could approach for waiving the inter- est. Section 30 of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 has also imposed similar embargo upon the Court's jurisdiction to interfere with the interest so payable by the borrower to the Bank under agreement, although the Court had authority to grant installment to the decreetal amount subject to some limitations.

(vii) In the case of Sonali Bank vs Messrs Beg and Beg Jute Incorporated Ltd. reported in 17 BLD AD 313, where defendant prayer for waiver of panel interest on the basis of Bangladesh Bank recommendation dated 19-3-84 which High Court Division allowed but Appellate Division held :-

"We, therefore, hold that the High Court Division acted illegally is not holding that the plaintiff-appellant was entitled to interest pendente lite. i.e. from the date of the institution of the suit upto the date of the passing of the decree."

(viii) In the case of Elite Lamps Ltd vs Bangladesh, 61 DLR 641 it has been held that, it is now a settlement principle of law that Article J 02 of the Constitution can be invoked only where the petitioner's right has undisputedly accrued under the Constitution or under any other legal instrument and, such as, has not been given effect to. In aforesaid letter dated 29-9-1992 Annexure B to the Writ Petition is not a legal instrument creating legal right for the petitioner for waiver of 100% interest and other benefit as has been observed above. It is only lays down the policy of the Government making recommendation for waiver of such interest without creating any legal right.

It has further been held that it appears to us this recommendation is not legal instrument created any legal right for the petitioner so as to implement it through a Court. Similarly, we have examined the recommendation of Parliamentary Committee (Annexure-Q to the Writ Petition) it appears to us that this recommendation is neither a legal instrument having force of law nor a law creating any legal right to the petitioner.

(ix) In Writ Petition No. 2044 of 2007 a Division Bench of this Court by judgment dated 18- 2-2009 held that it may be true that one of the objectives of introducing the Investment Board Act, 1989 is to extend assistance to Sick Industries. The formation of "Sick Industries Rehabilitation Cell" and other committees for the purpose of identification of sick industries and making recommendations for resolving the problems of sick industries also may have basis in the Board of Investment Act, 1989.But the recommendations of this Cell and Commit- tees have no force of law and are not binding on the loan granting banks and financial institution unless and until these recommendations are accepted by the government and proper directions are made by the government for implementation of these recommendations.

(x) In the judgment disposing of writ-petition No. 6270 of 2003 and writ-petition No. 3992 of 1999 a Division Bench of the High Court Division held:

"There is no legal obligation on the part of the loan granting banks not to initiate the legal proceedings or to institute a suit for realization of the outstanding dues and the recommendations and the policy as formulated in the notification dated 6-3-97 for settlement of the dues out of the Court for the purpose of' rehabilitation of the sick industries are not bindingupon the respondent bank and the respondent will proceed for realization of the duesunder the law namely "the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003."

(xi) The Honorable Appellate Division also in acase reported in 7 BLT (AD) 313 has held thus:

"The recommendation of a Cabinet Committee cannot be enforced through a writ for the simple reason that it is not law. It is as simple as that.

However, we do not think that more discussion is necessary to answer the first question raised in this writ-petition for determination: which we have already mentioned above. From the above discussion it is clear that the recommendations of "Sick Industries Rehabilitation Cell" and other Committees formed by the government being mere recommendations and being, admittedly, not accepted by the government, are not bindings on the loan granting banks and financial institutions. So there is no impediment for the banks and financial institutions in filing and proceeding with the suits and other legal proceedings against the sick industries for realization of outstanding loans. These recommendations do not create any legal obligation for the loan granting banks and financial institutions not to initiate any legal proceeding or suit for realization of the outstanding dues from the defaulter borrowers. These recommendations having no force of law are not enforceable also through writ jurisdiction of this, Court."

(xii) In FA No. 422 of 1998 Janata Bank vs Md Ibrahim Khalil a Division Bench, of this Court by judgment and order dated 9-3-2008 held as :

"It appears from the impugned 'judgment and decree that the plaintiff claimed that' the defendant took loan of Taka 20,060 on 21-9- 1988 from the plaintiff-Bank but thereafter he did not repay the loan as per terms and conditions of the sanction letter and ultimately the amount of loan, principal with interest and penal interest admittedly stood at Taka 33,223 as on 29-12-1993. Plaintiff filed the suit for recovery of the aforesaid amount, from the defendant with interest there on till its realization. It appears from the impugned judgment and decree that the Court below although decreed the suit as a whole to be paid by six installments but did not allow interest upon the decretal amount till its realization."

14. From the discussion made in the foregoing paragraphs and the decisions referred to as above, it is clear that by now it is a well established principle of law that policy guide line, recommendations, etc. not being law cannot be enforced through Court.

15. In this connection articulation of section 8 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain,1990(Act No. IV of 1990) needs be mentioned which reads as follows:

৮। ঝণের কিস্তি অর্থ খণ আদালত ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা কিস্তিতে পরিশোধ করা যথাযথ বরিয়া বিবেচনা করিলে উহা পরিশোধের জন্য ডিক্রিদারের বিনা সম্মাতিতে এক বৎসরের

অধিক সময় দিতে পারিবেন না।"

<u>16. Section 8 of the aforesaid Act No. 4 of 1990 was subsequently amended by Act No. 25 of 1992 as under :—</u>

<u>৭। ১৯৯০ সনের ৪নং আইনের ধারা ৮ এর সংশোধন উক্ত আইনের ধারা ৮ এর শেষে দাড়ির পরিবর্তে একটি “কোলনঃ প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে এবং তৎপর নিন্নবূপ শর্তাংশ</u>

সঙযোজিত হইবে, যথা:

<u>"তবে শর্ত থাকে যে. কোন কিস্তি মঞ্জুরকালে আদালত ডিক্রি সম্পাদিত চুক্তিতে নির্ধারিত সুদের হার সুদ প্রদানের নির্দেশ দিবে"</u>

<u>In view of the above it is apparent that the Court is not empowered or authorized to waive interest charged on the, amount under claim as per agreement executed between the judgment debtor and the financial institution i.e. the plaintiff-Bank till its realization. The contemplation of the aforesaid provision of law is clear and unambiguous that the, Court cannot waive such interest and it is the Bank itself who could waive such interest to whom the defendant could approach for waiving the interest. Section 30 of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 has also imposed similar embargo upon the Court's jurisdiction to interfere with the interest so payable by the borrower to the Bank under agreement, although the Court had authority to grant installment to the decretal amount subject to some limitations.</u>

17. In consideration all these decisions above, we are of the view that under Code of Civil Procedure the Court can waive interest but Court has no authority to, waive interest under special law i.e. under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Special Law is directed towards a special subject, a special class of objects and gives rise to special cause of action and self provides for the method of enforcement of rights conferred by that Act i.e. a code complete in" itself. Therefore, Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 or 2003 is a special law. Since the act do not permit waiving of interest, Court cannot waive interest either penal or general. We are of the view that interest can be waived only by the Bank if the borrower can make proper representation to the Bank.

18.	In the result, the appeal is allowed.

19.	The judgment and decree passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Judge, Artha Rin Adalat Kushtia in Artha Rin Suit No. 131 of 1993 with cost is set aside so far as it relates to not allowing pendente lite. Interest pendente lite will be paid in Money Suit' till realisation of decreetal amount.

Send down the lower Court record.

Communicate this order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Moyeenul lslam Chowdhury J : A Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the petitioners being employees of Bangladesh Biman Flight Catering Centre (BFCC) should not be governed by the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations, 1979 and absorbed as such in the service of Biman from the dates of their respective appointments entitling them to retirement and others benefits in line with those of the permanent Biman employees working in BFCC and why clause (d) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Organization Order No. 13 of 1989 dated 11-11-1989 (Annexure-'D') issued under the signature of the respondent No.3 purporting to discriminate between the regular employees of Bangladesh Biman Corporation who were transferred from the Cabin Facilities Department to the newly-established BFCC and the newly-recruited employees of BFCC should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why the respondents should not be directed to regularize the service of the petitioners in Biman pursuant to the recommendations of various inquiry committees formed from time to time with all Biman service facilities and allowances including retirement benefits and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The petitioners' case, as set out in the Writ Petition, in short, is as follows: The petitioners are the employees of the Biman Flight Catering Centre (BFCC) appointed by the BFCC Management against different posts on contractual basis. Anyway, initially BFCC was established as a project approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) in its meeting held on 16-8-1988. In course of time, BFCC became an integral part of Bangladesh Biman which was established under the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance of 1977. With the establishment of BFCC in 1989 at Zia International Airport, now renamed as Hazrat Shah Jalal international Airport, Biman Management abolished the Cabin Facilities Department of Bangladesh Biman which consisted of two sections, namely, Field Service and Catering Section by Organization Order No. 13 of 1989 dated 11-11-1989 issued under the signature of the respondent No. 3 and thereby transferred all the existing employees of the Cabin Facilities Department of BFCC. Clause (b) of the said Organization Order No. 13 of 1989 provides that the employees transferred to BFCC would be functionally and administratively accountable to BFCC Management and on transfer, their service would be governed by the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations, 1979 (in short, the Regulations of 1979) and they would continue to receive salaries, allowances and other facilities of Biman as per their terms of engagement. Although the employees transferred to BFCC are entitled to all Biman facilities and benefits as per clause (b) of the Organization Order No. 13 of 1989, but clause (d) of the said Organization Order discriminates the newly-recruited employees of BFCC in the sense that the will be governed by BFCC rules and service regulations and that Biman service facilities and benefits will not be admissible to them.

3. Under the administrative and financial policy formulated by BFCC Board, BFCC Management has been recruiting employees since 1990 against different posts on contractual basis within the permanent organizational set-up of BFCC approved by the Biman Authority. The petitioners being employees of BFCC were primarily appointed on contractual basis for a period of 3(three) or 5 (five) years in different capacities. Subsequently, their contractual periods were extended or renewed for further periods. In this way, some of the petitioners have already completed about 15 (fifteen) years of service in BFCC. However, initially the petitioners were paid consolidated salaries by the authority and afterwards pursuant to the declaration of the new National Pay Scale by the Government in 1991, BFCC Management determined their Pay Scale in line with the Pay Scale applicable to the permanent Biman officers/employees. The petitioners received their salaries accordingly. By the Administrative Order No. 02 of 1998 dated 21-6-1998, BFCC Management approved the implementation of the new National Pay Scale of 1997 to all BFCC contractual employees in line with the Biman Administrative Order No. 07 of 1998 dated 5-4-1998. The Administrative Order No. 02 of 1998 came into force with effect from 1-7-1997 and since then, the petitioners had been receiving their salaries in the new Pay Scale of 1997. But unlike the permanent Biman officers/employees, they are not entitled to other allowance and retirement benefits like pension, provident fund, medical facility etc. On perusal of the appointment letter of a contractual employee and that of a permanent Biman employee, it appears that though both the employees have been appointed in the same Pay Group and primarily on contractual basis under almost identical terms and conditions and are being paid in the same Pay Scale, the terms and conditions of the permanent employee's service will be governed by the Rules of 1979 and his service will be regularized with effect from the date of this contractual appointment subject to his satisfactory performance during the period of contract. On the other hand, the terms and conditions of the contractual employee's service will be governed as per the service agreement and the Orders, Instructions etc. issued from time to time by BFCC. The BFCC Board was reconstituted by the Office Order No.7 of 1995 dated 29-3-1995 where in it was stated that the Board would, inter alia frame Service Rules or Regulations for the newly- recruited contractual employees; but unfortunately no Service Rules or Regulations have yet been framed by the BFCC Board. In the mean time, by issuing various Administrative Order the BFCC Management approved/introduced different policies and service benefits for the contractual employees like enhancement of salaries and allowances, gratuity benefit etc. From Memos dated 1-6-2000 and 12- 9-2001 issued under the signature of the Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, it is clear that for regularization of BFCC contractual employees, the Ministry asked the respondent No. 2 to provide it with necessary papers/documents, but unfortunate the Biman authority did not respond thereto. Because of reluctance of the Biman authority, they could not be regularized in spite of the issuance of the said two Memos dated 1-6-2000 and 12-9-200 I by the Government. It was stated in the agenda of a Biman ED meeting signed on 30-12-2001 that by reason of the dual management system in BFCC and the discriminatory terms and conditions governing the service of the contractual employees, the smooth functioning of BFCC was being hampered and, as such, it was recommended that the contractual employees be regularized and governed under the Regulations of 1979. But the said recommendation went unheeded. However, in an inquiry report dated 28-1-2002 submitted by a three-member committee of the Government, it has been stated that the appointment of contractual employees against the permanent setup of Biman and extension of their service for indefinite duration are not consistent with the policies of the Government. The said committee recommended that both the regular Biman employees and contractual employees of BFCC be administered under a uniform regime and that the contractual employees be absorbed in the service of Biman. Alternatively, the committee recommended to convert BFCC into a company and administer all its employees according to the Company Law. But strangely enough, no positive step has been taken by the Biman authority for implementation of the recommendation as yet. In another inquiry report dated 27-10-2004 submitted by a one-member committee of the Government, it has been stated that since the regular and contractual employees of BFCC are not receiving equal treatment with regard to salaries and other service benefits, there exists a disappointing atmosphere in BFCC causing a feeling of deprivation among the contractual employees to the detriment of the smooth functionality of BFCC. So this committee also recommended that the contractual employees of BFCC be regularized in the service of Biman. Lastly, on 9-1-2005, a five-member commit- tee headed by the General Manager (Administration), Biman submitted a report wherein it was recommended that in order to remove complications as regards promotion of the regular Biman employees and contractual employees of BFCC might be converted into a company under the control of the Biman Corporation.

4. As per Office Order No. 7 of 1995 dated 29-3-1995, the BFCC Board is obligated to frame Service Regulations/Rules for the newly-recruited contractual employees of BFCC; but no such Regulations/Rules have been framed as yet, albeit they are getting various service benefits/facilities under different Administrative Orders issued from time to time. While Regulation 4(1) of the Regulations of 1979 provides that the contractual employees shall be bound thereby, clause (d) of the Organization Order No. 13 of 1989 discriminates between the regular employees and the contractual employees by indicating that the Biman service facilities and benefits will not be applicable to the contractual employees. This being the scenario cause (d) of the Organization Order No. 13 of 1989 dated 11-11-1989 is arbitrary and violative of the fundamental rights of the petitioners. It is worthy or notice that both the regular and contractual employees of BFCC were appointed under the same terms and conditions and as per the Regulations of 1979. but the service of the contractual employees is governed by various Administrative Orders of BFCC and not by the Regulations of 1979 and such contractual appointments of the petitioners are against the provisions of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance of 1977. The impugned Organization Order No. 13 of 1989 is ultra vires the power of the Director (Administration) of Biman Corporation. BFCC being a permanent set up within the organizational structure of Biman, the service of its contractual employees should be governed by the Regulations of 1979. So the issuance of Administrative Orders by BFCC Management to govern the service of the contractual employees without the approval of the Government is violative of the provisions of Section 30 of the Ordinance of 1977. The contractual employees of BFCC are enjoying almost all the service benefits like the regular Biman employees and, as such, they should be regularized as per the recommendations of various inquiry committees for efficient performance of their functions. Against this backdrop, the Biman authority is legally mandated to regularize the petitioners in the service of Biman.

5. In the Supplementary Affidavit dated 16- 11-2005 filed on behalf of the petitioners, it has been mentioned that as per the relevant Government policy, all revenue posts transferred from development projects shall be made permanent after three years.

6. In the Supplementary Affidavit dated 12-5- 2010 filed on behalf of the petitioners, it has been stated that over the years, BFCC has become an integral part of Biman and this is why, it is managed and controlled by Biman. The contractual employees of BFCC will continue to work till attainment of 57 years and they are retiring from service just like the permanent/regular employees of BFCC. Only the permanent employees of Biman are entitled to service benefits like gratuity and various types of leave as per the Regulations of 1979; but never the less the contractual employees of BFCC are also getting these benefits which show that they are being treated as permanent employees of Biman for all practical purposes. Further, the Administrative Order concerning payment of gratuity to the contractual employees of BFCC also contemplates that they would go on working for an indefinite duration and be entitled to gratuity only on satisfactory completion of 7 years of service.

7. The respondent no. 2 has contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition. His case as set out in the Affidavit-in-Opposition, in short runs as follows:

8. Clause (d) of the Bangladesh Biman Organization Order No. 13 of 1989 does not discriminate between the regular employees of Bangladesh Biman and the newly-recruited employees of BFCC. It is specifically stated that the newly- recruited employees of BFCC have been appointed on contractual basis and that these employees have agreed under their contracts with BFCC that their terms and conditions of service will be governed as per their agreements with BFCC and as per the Service Regulations, Orders and Instructions issued from time to time by BFCC. As the petitioners are contractual appointees, they are bound by the terms and conditions of their contracts and, as such. they are not entitled to enjoy all the benefits admissible to the permanent/regular employees of Biman. BFCC not only has its own Administrative and Financial Rules, but also has a separate Organogram (Organizational Chart). The terms and conditions or the service of the petitioners are prescribed by BFCC and not by Biman, Over and above, the salaries of the petitioners are paid not by Biman, but by BFCC. The allegation of discrimination by the petitioners in view of non-application or the Regulations of 1979 is clearly misconceived. The petitioners have been receiving gratuity, medical allowance and other facilities under their contracts with BFCC. Besides, they are currently receiving certain benefits/allowances that are not available to the permanent employees of Biman,So the contractual employees form a distinct class by themselves. The petitioners' employment is currently regulated by various Administrative Orders and Instructions issued by BFCC and therefore they have not been in any way prejudiced by the fact that no Service Regulations are in place. The inquiry committee which submitted its report on 28-1-2002 was set lip to inquire into certain audit objections. It was not set up for the purpose of reporting on the alleged differences between the terms and conditions of service of the contractual employees of BFCC and those of the permanent employees of Biman. The inquiry report dated 27-10-2004 was in relation to the presence of a nail in the food supplied by BFCC to Qatar Airways and the observations made therein vis-a-vis the service conditions of the two sets of employees are uncalled-for, unjustified and unwarranted.

9. In the Supplementary Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 16-3-2006 filed on behalf of the respondent No.2, it has been averred that the petitioners have all been directly recruited by BFCC on contractual basis and the permanent employees of Biman working in BFCC have been appointed on deputation. Originally BFCC was a project of Biman. Biman is currentiy running a Poultry Complex which is manned by direct recruits on contractual basis as well as the permanent employees of Biman working on deputation there. The Deputy General Manager of BFCC is a permanent furtctionary of Biman working on deputation in BFCC. The contractual periods of the petitioners have been extended/renewed from time to time by BFCC.
